solution_latex: Equal ranks mean the augmented column introduces no contradiction.
common_mistake: A rectangular system can be consistent.

question_latex: For an m×n matrix, rank plus nullity equals
solution_latex: Rank-nullity for the map from Rⁿ uses domain dimension n.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A row [0 0 0 | 5] in an augmented echelon matrix means
solution_latex: It represents the impossible equation 0=5.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Elementary row operations preserve
options: the solution set of an augmented system
the determinant unchanged in every case
solution_latex: Each row operation produces an equivalent system.
common_mistake: Row swaps/scalings can change determinant.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If a square n×n matrix has rank n, then Ax=b has
options: a unique solution for every b
only the zero solution for every b
solution_latex: Full rank makes A invertible.
common_mistake: For nonzero b, the unique solution need not be zero.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A pivot column in row echelon form corresponds to
solution_latex: Pivot positions identify leading/basic variables.
common_mistake: Non-pivot columns correspond to free variables.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Which operations are valid elementary row operations?
options: Multiply a row by a nonzero scalar
Add a multiple of one row to another
Square every entry in a row
solution_latex: The first three are reversible linear row operations. Entrywise squaring is nonlinear.
common_mistake: A row scale cannot use zero.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: The null space of A contains
options: solutions of Ax=b for every b
solution_latex: Null(A) is defined as all domain vectors mapped to zero.
common_mistake: Null vectors live in the domain.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If Ax=b has one solution xp, then every solution is
solution_latex: If Ax=b and Axp=b, then A(x−xp)=0.
common_mistake: The homogeneous component describes all freedom.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Row rank and column rank of a matrix are
solution_latex: Both equal the matrix rank for every finite matrix.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A 4×7 matrix has rank 3. Enter its nullity.
solution_latex: Nullity=7−3=4.
common_mistake: Use the number of columns.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A homogeneous system has 6 variables and 4 pivots. Enter its number of free variables.
solution_latex: Free variables=6−4=2.
common_mistake: Rows do not determine the count directly.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter rank of [[1,2],[2,4]].
solution_latex: The second row is twice the first and the matrix is nonzero.
common_mistake: Dependent rows reduce rank to one, not zero.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter nullity of the 3×3 identity matrix.
solution_latex: Identity has rank 3, so nullity is 0.
common_mistake: Only the zero vector maps to zero.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: The RREF of a 3×5 matrix has 2 pivots. Enter dimension of its row space.
solution_latex: Row-space dimension equals rank, the pivot count.
common_mistake: Nonzero RREF rows form a row-space basis.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter the rank of a nonzero 4×4 matrix whose every row is a scalar multiple of the first.
solution_latex: All rows span one nonzero direction.
common_mistake: Nonzero prevents rank zero.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A 3×4 matrix A has rank 3. Enter dimension of its left null space Null(Aᵀ).
solution_latex: Aᵀ has 3 columns and rank 3, so its nullity is 0; equivalently m−rank=3−3.
common_mistake: Left nullity uses number of rows of A.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If rank(A)=rank([A|b])=2 and A has 5 columns, enter the number of free variables.
solution_latex: The system is consistent and has 5−2=3 free variables.
common_mistake: Equal ranks establish consistency; columns minus rank gives freedom.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter rank of a 5×3 matrix with three linearly independent columns.
solution_latex: Independent columns give column-space dimension 3.
common_mistake: Rank cannot exceed the three columns.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A linear system in 4 unknowns has a unique solution. Enter nullity of its coefficient matrix.
solution_latex: Uniqueness means the associated homogeneous system has only zero solution.
common_mistake: Consistency alone would not force nullity zero.
